text.p: - Czech holding company ICEC nominated Siegfried Meysel as general manager of Slovenian paper factory Videm. ICEC bought Videm at an auction in March.
- Number of tourists at Slovenia's coast this week rose six percent compared to the same week in 1995.

- Slovenia is one of the most likely candidates for full NATO membership as it fulfils many conditions better than other states that entered the Partnership For Peace programme, Defence Minister Jelko Kacin said on Wednesday.
- Questionnaire finds that the biggest concerns of Slovenians are unemployment, improvement of the economy and living standards.
- Slovenia started a free-trade agreement with Latvia to increase trade between the two states, which currently stands at $2.8 million. A similar deal with Lithuania is expected to be signed soon.
- Ministry of Economic Activities to initiate a project aimed at lowering energy consumption in Slovenian homes.

- Experts researching an underground waste area in eastern Slovenia, where a Ljubljana hospital deposited radioactive waste in 1961, said they have already collected some 30 out of 72 barrels of waste.
- Financing of Slovenian municipalities is inadequate, mayors said in a protest letter to Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
